options.name: Battery plus an external 24 V DC input (tether hung from a boom)
options.what_it_changes: Adds a 24 V input at the tail base through a priority power path (LTC4417 class). It also adds a regeneration clamp at 27 V or below, a Category 1 E-stop that cuts both sources, a boom-hung tether and an equal-mass dummy pack (0.678 kg) for battery-free runs. The pack stays as the tail-base counterweight.
addresses: On tethered runs the bus comes from the supply, not the pack's 21.0-25.2 V swing. The record does not evaluate this as a knee-speed lever.
effect: The tether carries the peaks: about 6.2 A at 60 cm and 8.7 A at 75 cm, against means of 3.0 / 3.7 A. 5 m of SJOOW 16/2 drops 0.82 / 1.14 V at those peaks. [MATERIALS.md:§6/L230-233]

2 N of tether drag raises the brisk friction need on the narrow 60 cm picks from 0.73-0.75 to 0.78-0.85. A trailed 5 m cable drags 1.2-3.6 N, against a 7.1-7.2 N tip threshold. [MATERIALS.md:§6/L242-246]
options.mass_change: Not given for the input. The dummy pack is 0.678 kg for battery-free runs.
options.cost_change_nominal_high: About $0.2-0.4k for the input, power path, clamp and puck, plus $0.3-1.5k for a boom if the catch frame cannot carry it (estimates)
options.runtime_change: None on the battery. A plain contactor's 6 W coil would cost about 3.6 min at 60 cm.
risks_side_effects: The clamp must sit at or below 27 V because the 60 cm AK45 drives accept only 15-28 V. The supply's own over-voltage trip is at 27.6-32.4 V.
Tether drag and snag risk mean the cable is never trailed.
No practical breakaway connector releases below the tip threshold.
A balancer stronger than the hanging cable lifts the tail base.

options.name: Pad tread compound, measured on the owner's floors
options.what_it_changes: The pad tread material. Recommended: cast polyether polyurethane, 50-60 Shore A tread on a 70-80 A core, with 1.0-1.5 mm round studs.
effect: Expected PU static μ (source estimates): carpet 0.70-0.85; wood 0.8-0.9; ceramic tile 0.9-1.0; polished concrete 0.6-0.85 dry; laminate and vinyl 0.42-0.8, as low as about 0.50 on vinyl and 0.42 on laminate. Wear 23-40 mm³ DIN. [MATERIALS.md:§5/L171]

Against the 60 cm picks' needs (0.47-0.48 / 0.53-0.54 / 0.73-0.75): they walk and turn on carpet, wood, tile and polished concrete. They walk brisk on wood and tile but not on the lowest-grip carpet or concrete. They barely walk on vinyl (nominal walk only) and cannot walk on laminate. [ROUND2_REVIEW.md:§9/L599-607; MATERIALS.md:§5/L183]

Alternatives: natural gum or SBR 40 A has similar grip but ages (80-120 mm³). Silicone 30-40 A gives about 1.0 on clean smooth floors, is unknown on carpet, tears easily and picks up dust and lint. Neoprene gives no grip advantage. Hard pads of 90 A and up give 0.35-0.45 on carpet. [MATERIALS.md:§5/L171-175]
options.cost_change_nominal_high: Bench test about 1 day and $100 (estimate). The tread cost is not given separately.
risks_side_effects: Every μ is a literature estimate until the pad is measured at the robot's pad pressure (72-74 kPa at 60 cm) on the owner's floors, dry and dusty, before and after two hours of walking.
Stage 0 uses μ 0.54 (A16).
options.status: PU treads adopted (P21); the measurement is pending

addresses: Turn clearance against the 1.2-1.6 mm of round two
effect: The nominal walk needs 0.48-0.49 against 0.55-0.57 at base width (-13 %); brisk 0.75-0.77 against 0.85-0.87. Turns clear by 3.1-3.5 mm. Scorecard 0.694 / 0.689. [ROUND2_REVIEW.md:§7.4/L419-420, L430-435]

With the carpet-ready ankle drives (the picks), it needs 12-14 % less friction than the base-width carpet-ready bodies: 0.47-0.48 / 0.53-0.54 / 0.73-0.75 against 0.54-0.55 / 0.62-0.63 / 0.83-0.86. It draws 1.5-1.6 W less (69.3-69.6 W), so it runs about 1 min longer. The knee's Fr 0.05 ratio falls from 0.95-0.97 to 0.93-0.95. Scorecard 0.703 / 0.699 against 0.675 / 0.658. [ROUND2_REVIEW.md:§7.6/L484-489]
options.mass_change: About 0: +0.003 kg against the round-two narrow body; -0.01 / -0.02 kg against base-width carpet-ready
options.cost_change_nominal_high: +$2 / +$4 against the round-two narrow body; -$11 / -$18 and -$17 / -$29 against base-width carpet-ready
risks_side_effects: Turn gaps are 3.4 mm in the target turns against 4.0 mm at base width, and 3.0-3.1 mm against 3.4-4.0 mm in the 0.5 rad/s walking turn.
The narrowest stance is set by the hip hardware and turning, not by the shell (F16).
Stage 1 treats the turn gap (the pelvis plate's clearance to the same-side thigh) as not a hardware limit for the controller.
options.applies_to: 60 cm. The 75 cm pick keeps the base stance; the 75 cm narrow bodies cleared the in-place turn by only 0.8-1.0 mm.

effect: 60-N-T-10: worst ratio knee 0.929 to hip pitch 0.798; knee speed 0.929 to 0.685. [round2/gait_tune/GAIT_TUNE.md:table/L7]

Tuned 60 cm walks: lift 0.080 H, duty 0.55, stride 0.713 / 0.725 H (from 0.80 H), crouch 0.070 H. Cadence 2.75 to 3.09 and 2.76 to 3.05 steps/s. Hard-floor toe clearance 23.1 to 16.2 mm and 22.9 to 16.1 mm. CoP margin 29.7 to 29.3 mm. Sway 0.103 to 0.090 H and 0.104 to 0.093 H. Peak CoM acceleration 3.21 to 3.03 and 3.22 to 3.05 m/s². Peak CoM acceleration stays about twice the spec's 1.5 m/s².

open_questions: Knee transmission: the record has no knee transmission or gear-ratio design. The only knee option is the RobStride 06 swap. The picks' X4-36-L knee has torque headroom (0.49-0.51 sustained, 0.33-0.34 peak; candidate JSONs) and the hip pitch, at 0.89-0.90, is the next speed limit. Mass, cost, packaging and reflected inertia of a lower-ratio knee are not in the record.

Supply voltage: Stage 0 and the Stage 1 envelope take no speed credit above a drive's nominal voltage (designlab/catalog.py L77-82; designlab/stage1/drive.py L32-35). With the X4-36-L knee and hip pitch rated at 24 V, a fuller pack or a higher bus cannot raise their modelled speed; only vendor curves or the Stage 2 bench could show a real gain. The record does not say how much of a run the 6S bus spends below 24 V.

Higher bus at 60 cm: the AK45-36 hip roll and thigh twist (15-28 V) and the clamp at 27 V or below cap the 60 cm bus. Swapping them for X4-36-L, as the 75 cm targeted body did, is not sized or packaged at 60 cm. 12S also needs other regulators (E7) and a bus capacitor and regeneration clamp (A11).

STAGE1_PLAN.md §5 L115 gives the Fr 0.05 knee requirement as 8.08-8.12 rad/s, but 60-N-H-10's own record needs 8.253 rad/s (knee 0.949 of 8.69 rad/s). At 22.2 V its knee would be about 1.03 of the limit, not about 1.00. Check the ledger note before quoting it for 60-N-H-10.

The Fr 0.05 walk's friction need with the stance-foot yaw moment was never screened: the turning screen covers only the nominal and brisk walks. The brisk walk already needs 0.73-0.75 at 60 cm, so the animal-like walk may be grip-limited on many floors even where the knee is within its limit. Stage 1 reports Fr 0.05 at μ 0.54, not gated.

The faster knee was tested only on the base-width carpet-ready bodies, not on the narrow picks. Its +15 % turn friction would undo most of the narrow stance's 12-14 % gain. A brisk walk with the carpet swing on a faster knee was never run.

Bigger feet were never run on the narrow carpet-ready picks. Ankle A already governs 60-N-H-10's target turns at 0.76, and the bigger feet raised the Tapered knee's Fr 0.05 ratio from 0.95 to 0.98 at base width. Pads x1.25 alone let the 60 cm bodies stand on medium pile according to refine.json, but the review text does not say so.

Gait tuning: the look of the tuned walk (about 3.1 steps/s, stride 0.71-0.73 H, crouch at the 0.07 H bound) is not assessed. Settings outside the search bounds were not explored, there is no controller test, and no carpet-swing version was tuned. The owner holds it as information only (P24).
No new nominal reference walk meeting the 0.12 H sway and 1.5 m/s² acceleration limits has been designed. Whether one exists within the 60 cm drives is unknown.

Pad μ on the owner's floors is unmeasured (estimates only; about a day and $100 to test). Silicone's about 1.0 on clean smooth floors, against its dust pickup and poor wear, is not evaluated as a vinyl or laminate option.

The materials levers (PA11 walls, 2.54 mm plates) were applied to 60-M-T-10 carpet-ready, not the picks, and were never simulated together. Their effect on grip, stop and push is not reported; the re-sized PA12 walls left the friction need essentially unchanged (0.634 to 0.640 in refine.json).

How to measure the '80 %': the record has no behaviour-coverage metric. The scorecard (P17 weights) scores margins and ties the 60 and 75 cm picks (0.703 / 0.699 against 0.702). The gap map needs the owner's list of behaviours and looks, with weights.
Body or controller labels await Stage 1's margin ledger and the decision-20 paired test. Stage 1's carpet falls so far come from a tracker fitted on hard floor only.
Powered jaw, head yaw and arms (P1) are outside the demonstrator's scope (P2). The record has no mass, cost or servo data for them at 60 cm.
Neck and tail servo loads at the spec's upper amplitudes (±0.15 rad head, ±0.2 rad tail), or for livelier motion, are not reported. Only the reference walk's ±0.05 / ±0.12 rad is.
Combined options (for example faster knee plus bigger feet plus PA11) were never run, so their interactions, such as foot mass against knee speed, are unknown.
The lighter Li-ion pack's sloped discharge was not assessed for its effect on bus voltage and knee speed, and the cassette redesign was not simulated.
Whether the 3.0-3.4 mm turn gaps survive manufacturing tolerance is not assessed. Stage 1 treats the gap as not a hardware limit for control.
Once the knee is fixed, the hip pitch (0.89-0.90 at Fr 0.05; about 0.97 at 22.2 V, derived) binds. The record has no hip-pitch-only upgrade at 60 cm; only blanket headroom, which fails clearance.
Whether the tethered supply can be set above 24 V, up to the 27 V clamp, to offset the 0.82 V cable drop at peaks is not stated.
All option costs and masses are model estimates with no quotes (carbon ±50 %). The 60 cm high-side estimate is already above P4's $20k.

Front reach against ZMP shift needed is 43.5 vs 52.2 mm on 60-N-T-10, 43.2 vs 51.8 mm on 60-N-H-10 and 62.8 vs 66.7 mm on 75-M-H-10. The 15 mm rear reach in decision 15 explains why the untuned tracker's ankle torque rolled the foot (G4). It does not bound the stop.

For the final picks the summed drive peaks are 116-118 W and 194 W, i.e. 5.7-5.8 A at 60 cm and 8.9 A at 75 cm with the auxiliaries. The picks' runtimes are 47.4-47.6 min and 36.7 min.

They also took RobStride 06 hip pitch and knee and X4-36-L ankles, and they failed clearance. The narrow headroom bodies swapped only the thigh twist. On the bodies that were run, the governing Fr 0.05 ratio goes from 0.95 / 0.97 (knee) to 0.90 (hip pitch): a 5-7 % drop, leaving about 10 % headroom, so the gain itself is not about 10 %.

problems.correct: This comes from ROUND2_REVIEW §14, written before Stage 1, and now holds only for carpet. The Stage 1 pilot walked all three bodies 40 strides (20 at μ 0.54). problems.correct: Only 3 starts per floor were tried. 60-N-T-10 was tested at the tuning start (the prototype's terms), not with fitted gains. Only 75-M-H-10 was tested at its G5 selection, and 60-N-H-10 is not reported.

missed.what: A cross-check judge estimated the Fr 0.05 friction need from SHA-matched rebuilds of the round-two bodies: μ 1.05-1.27 at 60 cm and 0.72-0.88 at 75 cm. That is above every PU floor estimate, so the animal-like walk at 60 cm is likely limited by grip, not only by knee speed. The same check found Fr 0.05 with the carpet lift overspeeds the knee on every body (1.22-1.36 at 60 cm). Open question 5's "never screened" is true only of the official screens.
missed.source: round2/CROSSCHECK.md behavior-risk judge, key risks (stance-foot spin; Fr 0.05 with the carpet lift)

missed.what: Autonomy and compute are a missing shortfall. None of P3's obstacle avoidance and person following, or P1's navigation and voice commands, is shown at any size, against BEHAVIOR_SPEC §3's targets. The Teensy safety firmware is unwritten, so a Linux crash does not end in a controlled stop. The HOG detector misses its deadline on ARM. The Pi 5 + AI HAT+ load and draw are unmeasured (A14). Voice and mapping are budgeted only for the 100-120 cm NVIDIA builds, not the 60 cm Pi 5.
missed.source: DECISION_LOG.md P1/L16, P3/L18, F7/L61, A14/L98; BEHAVIOR_SPEC.md §3 L43-60; COMPUTE.md L26-35, L59-66, L148-183

Ankle A already needs 1.74 N·m, and about 2.0 N·m with bigger feet.
